body.objective: Students will be able to identify the elements of music.
body.iCan: I can identify the elements of music.
successCriteria: I can name and define the elements of music
I can describe a piece using musical vocabulary
I can identify elements by ear
body.hook: Hum "Happy Birthday" slowly in a low voice, then fast and high. Same song, completely different feeling. Musicians describe these differences with a shared vocabulary: the elements of music.

vocabulary.definition: A sequence of pitches heard as a tune.
Two or more pitches sounding together, such as chords.
The pattern of long and short sounds and silences in time.
How loud or soft the music is.
The unique tone colour of a voice or instrument.
How many layers of sound there are and how they relate.
The structure of a piece, such as verse-chorus or ABA.

study.title: Listening Like a Musician
study.question: How can we describe any piece of music precisely?
study.passage:
Elements checklist: melody (stepwise or leaping, high or low), harmony (major or minor, simple or complex), rhythm (steady, syncopated), tempo (largo slow, andante walking, allegro fast), dynamics (pp, p, mp, mf, f, ff; crescendo, decrescendo), timbre (which instruments or voices), texture (monophonic one line, homophonic melody plus chords, polyphonic several independent lines), form (AB, ABA, verse-chorus).
Listening 1 (5 minutes): A solo voice singing a folk song unaccompanied. What is the texture? (Monophonic.)
Listening 2 (5 minutes): A pop song with verse and chorus. Map the form as you listen.
Listening 3 (5 minutes): A Bach fugue. Count the independent lines. (Polyphonic.)
Listening 4 (5 minutes): Excerpt from a film score. Describe dynamics and tempo changes and the mood they create.
Task (20 minutes): Choose a song you love. Write a "listening profile" using at least six elements and precise vocabulary instead of "it sounds good."
study.source: Original listening task written for this lesson; teachers choose recordings.

examples.title: Texture
examples.problem: A choir sings one melody together in unison. What is the texture?
examples.explore: What changes if a guitar plays chords underneath?

examples.title: Dynamics
examples.problem: The music grows gradually louder. What is the term?

examples.title: Timbre
examples.problem: Why does a flute and a trumpet sound different on the same note?
examples.answer: Different timbre from how each instrument makes sound
examples.explore: How would you describe each timbre?

examples.title: Form
examples.problem: A song goes verse, chorus, verse, chorus, bridge, chorus. Name the form.
examples.explore: What job does the bridge do?

practice.a: A sequence of pitches heard as a tune.
How loud or soft music is.
The tone colour of a voice or instrument.
Several independent melodic lines at once.

practice.q: What is the difference between rhythm and tempo?
practice.a: Rhythm is the pattern of durations; tempo is the speed of the beat.
A section, contrasting B section, return of A.

practice.q: How does minor harmony usually sound compared to major?
How can dynamics build tension in a film score?
practice.a: A long crescendo raises intensity before a climax.

practice.q: Why might a songwriter use a bridge?
practice.a: To add contrast before the final chorus.

practice.q: Describe the texture change when a band enters after a solo singer.
practice.a: It moves from monophonic to homophonic or thicker.

practice.q: Why use precise vocabulary instead of "it sounds good"?
practice.a: It explains exactly what creates the effect.

misconceptions: Thinking loud always means exciting and soft means sad
Thinking texture is about how the music feels to touch
exitTicket: Name the texture of a melody with chords.

test.title: Practice test: Identify the elements of music

items.q: Tempo is
options: B) the speed of the beat
items.answer: B) the speed of the beat

items.q: Dynamics describe
items.answer: D) loudness and softness

items.q: Timbre is
options: B) the tone colour of a sound
items.answer: B) the tone colour of a sound

items.q: A melody is
options: D) a sequence of pitches heard as a tune
items.answer: D) a sequence of pitches heard as a tune

items.q: A melody with chords underneath is
items.answer: B) homophonic

items.q: A gradual increase in volume is a
items.answer: B) crescendo

items.q: Allegro means
items.answer: B) fast

items.q: ABA form has
options: A) a return of the first section
items.answer: A) a return of the first section

items.q: A Bach fugue with several independent lines is
items.answer: C) polyphonic

items.q: Two songs use the same chords but sound different mainly because of
options: C) different melody, rhythm, timbre and tempo
items.answer: C) different melody, rhythm, timbre and tempo

items.q: A film composer builds tension before a climax most likely with
options: B) a long crescendo and faster rhythm
D) slower tempo and softer dynamics only
items.answer: B) a long crescendo and faster rhythm

items.q: Rhythm differs from tempo because rhythm is
options: B) the speed of the beat
items.answer: C) the pattern of durations

items.q: Name four elements of music.
items.answer: Melody, harmony, rhythm, tempo, dynamics, timbre, texture, form.

items.q: What does p mean in dynamics?
items.answer: Piano, soft.

items.q: Explain the three types of texture.
items.answer: Monophonic one line; homophonic melody plus chords; polyphonic several independent lines.

items.q: Describe the form of a typical pop song.
items.answer: Verse, chorus, verse, chorus, bridge, chorus.

items.q: Explain the difference between rhythm and tempo.
items.answer: Rhythm is the pattern of long and short sounds; tempo is speed.

items.q: Describe the timbre of an instrument you know.
items.answer: Answers vary.

items.q: Write a listening description of a song using four elements.
items.answer: Answers vary.

items.q: Explain how two elements work together to create mood in a piece.
items.answer: Answers vary.
